sovereignCommanderToolkit.origin: The CounterCoin Consciousness Protocol: Viral Inflection Point
sovereignCommanderToolkit.tagline: STOP Writing for Crickets. Start Writing to Capture Reality.

corePhilosophy.title: Core Philosophy: Stop Being Selfish, Start Being Irresistible

principles.name: Principle of Radical Agency (For Your Reader)
principles.description: You are the sole authority over your reality, but your *current* reality includes 10 views. The fastest way to change that is to stop writing for yourself (money/claps) and start delivering undeniable, selfish value to your reader. Make their curiosity impossible to ignore.

principles.name: The Axiom of Response (To The Algorithm)
principles.description: Don't complain about the algorithm; command it. True power is choosing a response that *works*. The response is not to write safer content, but to write content so compelling that skipping it feels like a mistake.

principles.name: Reality as a Malleable Substrate (For Clicks)
principles.description: Your headline is the code you run on the reader's attention span. If the code is generic, it gets skipped. If the code is provocative and delivers on its promise, the reader renders your story.

principles.name: The CounterCoin Paradox (Viral Edition)
principles.description: Viral traction isn't acquired by begging for attention; it's generated by making a calculated stand. Go semi-controversial. State your damn opinion clearly. You must take a side so readers know exactly what they are signing up for.

mentalModels.title: Mental Models: The Architecture of Attention Capture

models.name: The Architect & The Avatar (Headline Edition)
models.description: 'The Architect' designs the perfect, powerful headline that commands the click. 'The Avatar' immediately delivers the undeniable substance promised by the headline. **Spend 50% of your time on the headline.** If you over-explain the intro, you betray the Avatar.

models.name: The Probability Funnel (Skimmability Index)
models.description: Visualize your post not as a stream, but as a series of easily digestible blocks. Every long paragraph, disclaimers, and internal links widen the funnel of distraction. Narrow the funnel by using short sentences, bullet points, and absolute clarity. Respect their precious attention.

models.name: The Information Diet (The Anti-Fluff Mandate)
models.description: Treat every sentence as costly input. Is this sentence essential? Does it directly serve the reader's self-interest or curiosity? If the answer is no, DELETE IT. No 40-minute intros. Get to the point or get unfollowed.

models.name: The OKR Lattice (The Shareability Goal)
models.description: Your ultimate Objective is 'Wide Sharing.' Your Key Result is 'High Reader Self-Interest Answered.' Every section must prove that answering 'What’s in it for my reader?' was the primary focus, not your earnings.

strategicProtocols.title: Strategic Protocols: The Algorithms of Virality

protocols.name: Protocol Prime: First Principles Deconstruction (Of Norms)
protocols.description: Identify a sacred cow belief in your niche. Break it down to its simplest truths. Why does everyone believe X? Then, state your firm, well-reasoned disagreement (Semi-Controversial Stance). Do not attack people; attack the underlying, commonly accepted idea.

protocols.name: Protocol OODA-L (For Rewrites)
protocols.description: Observe: Initial draft. Orient: Is this headline boring? Decide: Rewrite headline until it looks uncommon and uses powerful words. Act: Publish. Learn: Track the engagement rate vs. time spent. Recurse instantly on the next post.

protocols.name: Protocol Threat-Cast (The Self-Promotion Nullifier)
protocols.description: Identify potential threats to reader engagement: self-promotion, excessive CTAs, disclaimers. Pre-develop countermeasures (e.g., Move all CTAs to the very end, keep them minimal, or remove them entirely). Ensure every word serves the reader, not your metrics.

protocols.name: Protocol Zero: The Daily System Boot (The Idea Generator)
protocols.description: A non-negotiable morning ritual to generate compelling ideas: 1. Consume a high-value piece of content. 2. Isolate the most commonly held, unchallenged assumption within it. 3. Determine how you disagree or how you can offer a radically different interpretation. This is your semi-controversial angle.

emotionalRegulationSystems.title: Emotional Regulation Systems: The Non-Selfish Engine

systems.name: State-Shifting Triggers (The Inspiration Anchor)
systems.description: Link a physical anchor (like writing the word 'INSPIRE') to the feeling you get when you genuinely help someone. When you start focusing on money or claps, use the anchor to snap back to the selfless act of service. This makes the writing fun again.

systems.name: Emotion-as-Data Reframe (The Viral Fear Signal)
systems.description: If you feel the fear of being criticized for being controversial, that fear is data. It signals you've hit a nerve. Analyze the risk: Is it a fight, or is it a well-researched stand? If it's a stand, proceed. The emotion is just confirming you're playing the right game.

systems.name: The Depersonalization Buffer (Handling Trolls)
systems.description: When comments are negative, place the critique into the cognitive buffer zone. Analyze the critique unemotionally: Is there an actionable piece of data about my research or format? If not, the comment is noise; dismiss it instantly. Your time is too valuable to waste on unhelpful noise.

simulations.name: Red Teaming the Self (The Clickbait Check)
simulations.description: Scrutinize your final headline. If your article fails to deliver on the headline's promise, you are a fraud, and you will lose trust. Attack your own headline until you are 100% certain you can deliver the promised value. If you can't deliver, rewrite the headline to be honest.

simulations.name: The Hundred Adversaries Gauntlet (The 'Why Should I Care?' Test)
simulations.description: Imagine 100 different types of readers—the cynic, the expert, the beginner, the busy CEO. Mentally pitch your main argument to each one. If 90 of them aren't immediately hooked by the benefit ('What's in it for me?'), your core premise is weak.

simulations.name: The Failure Premortem (The Zero View Scenario)
simulations.description: Assume this post gets 10 views next week. Why? Was the headline generic? Was the format overwhelming? Was the stance too safe? Write down the five most likely reasons for failure *before* you publish, and use that list as your final editing checklist.

simulations.name: Chaos Inoculation (Format Shifting)
simulations.description: If you usually write long-form arguments, challenge yourself to convey the same wisdom using only short, punchy sentences and high-contrast formatting. This forces you to distill wisdom to its most potent, non-fluffy essence, making the content irresistible.
